long_biography.plain_text:
At Beauport in Gloucester, Massachusetts, lawyer Charles McCann and his wife Helena helped preserve an interior designer's unusual home. They acquired Henry Davis Sleeper's house and collections in 1935, when other prospective buyers intended to disperse its contents. The couple kept most rooms and their carefully arranged objects intact.

Their main alteration was the China Trade Room, which they adapted for entertaining. They hired French & Co. to introduce a marble mantel, a crystal chandelier and more formal furniture, while retaining the Chinese wallpaper and gilded balconies. The room still displays their alterations, alongside the largely preserved interiors created by Sleeper.
